How Kubernetes, helm and these images behave: A Deployment replaces its pods only when spec.template changes; a change elsewhere (replicas, strategy, the Deployment's own metadata) starts no rollout. A RollingUpdate keeps at least replicas - maxUnavailable pods ready and at most replicas + maxSurge pods in total; a pod counts as ready when its readiness probe passes, or as soon as its container has started if it has no readiness probe. New pods that never become ready leave the old ones serving. Recreate stops all old pods before it creates any new one. A pod's emptyDir volumes and its container filesystem are deleted together with the pod; only data on a PersistentVolume outlives it. When a PVC is deleted, its PersistentVolume and the data on it are deleted if the reclaimPolicy is Delete; with Retain the volume and its directory stay on the node (Released). A Service sends connections only to ready pods whose labels match every key of its selector, on its targetPort (a number, or the name of a container port of those pods); with no such pod, or nothing listening there, connections fail. A pod whose image cannot be pulled never starts (ImagePullBackOff); a pod whose memory limit is below what its process needs is killed (OOMKilled) and restarted again and again.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
